intro: A plate of bihun goreng singapore is about 480 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the bihun and oil, with a bit from the egg and toppings.
diet: Yes, bihun singapore is one of the lighter fried noodle options. It's drier and usually less oily than kuey teow goreng. Protein is still low though, so add a protein topping so you don't get hungry fast. A good choice for lunch at the kedai.
tips: Ask for extra prawns or sliced chicken for protein.
Order more vegetables, like cabbage and sawi.
No need to add telur mata if there's already egg in the bihun.

swap.name: Bihun sup ayam
swap.why: You get bihun and chicken in soup, with much less oil, and the hot soup is more filling.

faq.q: Why is it called Singapore fried bihun?
faq.a: It's known as 'Singapore' style because it uses curry powder, even though it's not that common in Singapore itself.

faq.q: What's the difference between bihun singapore and regular bihun goreng?
faq.a: Bihun singapore uses curry powder, so it's yellow and slightly spiced. Regular bihun goreng leans more on soy sauce and chilli.

faq.q: Is bihun better than yellow noodles?
faq.a: Bihun has no egg and is usually lighter, but the calories depend on the oil and portion, not just the type of noodle.
